claim_decisions.reason: Retain bounded source-supported finding with vintage and causal limitations; no extrapolation to 2026 or evaluated impact.
claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2025-04-01 reports: In the 2023/24 season, meteorological drought lasted five months in Machinga, Mangochi, Zomba and Chikwawa, and four months in Chitipa, Nsanje, Dedza, Phalombe, Chiradzulu and Thyolo; additional southern and central districts had dry spells through much of the season.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2025-04-01 reports: For the 2023/24 season, DoDMA data in the report count 17,033 households affected by floods in Karonga and Nkhotakota; all recorded hazards affected 21,333 households.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2024-09-04 reports: The assessment links El Niño income stress to children joining guardians' casual work, school absenteeism and child labour.

claim_decisions.reason: Retain bounded source-supported finding with vintage and causal limitations; no extrapolation to 2026 or evaluated impact.
claim_decisions.statement: The July 2024 UN assessment cites a rapid gender analysis linking deprivation to exploitation risk and weak local protection services; Machinga recorded 286 child marriages in January–May 2024 versus 162 a year earlier.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: Reported cases, not incidence or a drought-attributable effect. The report's 'doubling' description is not arithmetically supported by 286 versus 162 and is omitted; underreporting and comparison methods remain uncertain.
claim_decisions.locator: Physical PDF p.25, printed p.25, protection discussion citing El Niño Rapid Gender Analysis.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2024-09-04 reports: Drought lengthened women's water-collection journeys; women, girls and people with disabilities were excluded from key response-governance structures.

claim_decisions.reason: Retain bounded source-supported finding with vintage and causal limitations; no extrapolation to 2026 or evaluated impact.
claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2025-04-07 reports: The CCA reports 20,000+ people displaced by March 2024 floods in Karonga and Nkhotakota; about 400 households remained displaced in Nsanje, Chikwawa, Zomba and Nkhotakota; early camp closures prompted returns to unrepaired, flood-exposed homes.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: A 2024–2025 account of flood displacement and incomplete recovery, not a current caseload or a violence mechanism.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2025-04-07 reports: After dry spells and food insecurity, mostly male members of drought-affected Southern Region households moved semi-voluntarily for casual work in Blantyre, Mzuzu, Lilongwe, Rumphi or Mzimba.

claim_decisions.reason: Retain bounded source-supported finding with vintage and causal limitations; no extrapolation to 2026 or evaluated impact.
claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2025-04-07 reports: The CCA warns climate-driven mobility may intensify scarce-land competition and migrant–host tensions; it also reports households moving for arable land and fishers seeking grounds along Lake Malawi.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: Conditional national scenario, no named locality or measured host–migrant conflict. Mobility can improve livelihoods and does not inherently create violence.

claim_decisions.statement: UNICEF's January 2026 report says 11 districts exceeded 2025 severe-wasting projections, naming Neno, Nsanje and Chikwawa; these are service/planning indicators, not district prevalence estimates.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2026-01-26 reports: UNICEF reported deep-water systems in drought-affected schools and communities in Nsanje and Neno reaching over 12,000 people, more than half women and girls; improved sanitation reached 36,569 people in Chikwawa and Nsanje.

pathways.climate_pressure: El Niño-related drought and livelihood/food insecurity in the 2023/24 period.
pathways.documented_impact: Household economic stress and harmful coping pressures affected children and women.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Unequal control over relief/resources, weak community protection services and economic dependence.
pathways.possible_consequence: The assessment reports exploitation risks and rising reported child marriage; Machinga counts illustrate reporting, not prevalence or attribution.
alternative_explanations: Food-price inflation, accumulated shocks, reporting/access changes and pre-existing gender inequality also matter.
pathways.uncertainty: A source-stated risk mechanism synthesized in July 2024, not a climate-attributable violence estimate or a 2026 protection assessment.
resilience_factors: Accessible protection services and inclusive response decisions address identified constraints; effectiveness is not established here.
pathways.compact_statement: The 2024 assessment links livelihood stress and unequal resource access with protection risks, with a historical Machinga reporting example; causal attribution is unresolved.

gaps: The Machinga marriage counts are reported cases from secondary rapid-analysis evidence, not prevalence, and cannot identify an El Niño causal effect.
No inspected source establishes current host–migrant violence or evaluates whether training, plans or parametric payouts reduced long-term vulnerability.

executive_assessment.text: Named 2023/24 drought and flood examples distinguish meteorological conditions from household losses and later recovery constraints.
Economic stress, unequal control over resources and weak protection services form a plausible protection-risk mechanism, but reported cases and forecasts are not causal estimates.
Dzaleka/host payouts and district preparedness outputs are documented without assuming sustained resilience gains.
